senses.gloss: (b. h.) to fill, saturate; to drink freely.—Part. pass. שָׁכוּר; f. שְׁכוּרָה.
units: <cite ref="Taanit 22b:19">Taan. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>לא ש׳ ולא צמאה וכ׳</he> that the soil be neither soaked nor thirsty, but between the two extremes.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 35:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXXV</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 51:21">Is. LI, 21</cite>) <he>וממה את ש׳ מן הצרות וכ׳</he> and wherefrom art thou drunk? From the troubles, but not from too much wine; a. e.

<cite ref="Eruvin 64b:13">Erub. 64ᵇ</cite> <he>דרך … מְשַׁכַּרְתּוֹ</he> walking (after drinking) makes him unsteady, and sleep makes him drunk; <cite ref="Taanit 17b">Taan. 17ᵇ</cite>. Erub. l. c. <he>רביעית … מְשַׁכֵּר</he> one fourth of a Log of Italian wine intoxicates.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:4">Cant. R. to I, 4</cite> <he>ועשו … ושִׁכְּרַתּוֹ וכ׳</he> they made a great feast, and she made him drink more than enough; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 15">Yalk. Gen. 15</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Ketubot 8b:13">Keth. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>התחילו … ומִשְׁתַּכְּרִין וכ׳</he> when they began to drink (at the mourners’ meals) and get intoxicated &c.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 6:1">Esth. R. to III, 9</cite> <he>אכלו ושתו ונִשְׁתַּכְּרוּ וכ׳</he> they ate and drank, and became drunk, and acted disgracefully.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10:8">Num. R. s. 10<sup>8</sup></cite> <he>דברים שלא יִשְׁתַּכֵּר מהם</he> things from which one cannot become intoxicated; a. fr.
